questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This image shows the aorta, which is an elastic artery. The tunica media of this vessel contains elastic lamellae, or laminae, which are concentric layers of fenestrated sheets of elastic tissue. They provide the "shock absorber" for the systolic phase of heart contraction, while their rebound helps maintain arterial pressure.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The tunica adventitia is the outermost layer of vessels and often blends with the surrounding connective tissue through which the vessel is passing. The adventitia consists of dense irregular connective tissue. In larger vessels the adventitia contains small vessels, the vasa vasorum, which nourish the vessel wall.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the oval.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The annulus fibrosus lies at the junction of the membranous septum and the atrioventricular valve. This ring of dense connective tissue is the part of the cardiac skeleton that encircles each valve. The annulus provides support for that valve and anchorage for the insertion of cardiac muscle fibers. The connective tissue core of each valve leaflet is continuous with the annulus fibrosus.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the vessel indicated by the square.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Arterioles have a narrow lumen with a relatively thick wall consisting of up to three layers of smooth muscle cells in the tunica media.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The atrioventricular bundle lies in the connective tissue beneath the endocardium. The A-V bundle divides to form the right and left bundle branches. Purkinje cells, modified cardiac muscle fibers, leave the bundle branches to supply the cardiac muscle fibers of the myocardium.

alternativas.texto: Muscular portion of the interventricular septum

questoes.enunciado: Identify the vessels shown in these images.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Fenestrated capillaries are characterized by fenestrations or pores that are spanned by a diaphragm. Fenestrations facilitate transport across the endothelium in organs where abundant and rapid transport occurs, such as in the digestive and endocrine systems. Fenestrated capillaries are also present in renal glomeruli, but these lack diaphragms.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the vessels indicated by the arrows in these images.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Capillaries are lined only by an endothelium and its basal lamina. Continuous capillaries are composed of one or two endothelial cells and the surrounding basal lamina. Occluding junctions unite adjacent cells and because of their narrow lumen, these capillaries only allow erythrocytes pass through in single file. Continuous capillaries are the most prevalent type as seen in this adipose tissue.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the specific layer indicated by the arrows

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The epithelium lining all blood vessels is classified as a simple squamous epithelium, with a unique name, endothelium. The endothelium is a component of the tunica intima, which also includes the underlying subendothelial connective tissue.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the white blood cells in this image.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Eosinophils are granular leucocytes with a heterochromatic, bilobed nucleus and bright eosinophilic granules that fill the cytoplasm. Like neutrophils, eosinophils function in tissues and readily exit the blood stream. Eosinophils play a role in allergic reactions and parasitic infections as well as phagocytosis.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The internal elastic lamina lies just beneath the subendothelial connective tissue of the tunica intima. It is similar in structure to lamellae of elastic arteries seen in the tunica media.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The tunica intima faces the blood and is lined by an inner layer of specialized simple squamous epithelium termed endothelium. Underlying the endothelium is a thin connective tissue layer. Beneath the connective tissue is the internal elastic lamina; this lamina, lacking in the smallest arteries and all but the larger veins, consists of a single, broad, fenestrated elastic sheet.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the vessel, seen here in cross section, that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. A feature of large veins, like the vena cava shown here, is a significant amount of smooth muscle in the tunica adventitia. Smooth muscle fibers in the adventitia are oriented longitudinally, thus they are seen in cross section. Smooth muscle fibers in the media are arranged circularly and thus are seen in longitudinal section. This stain for elastin clearly shows the internal elastic lamina and elastic fibers throughout the adventitia.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In arteries, the tunica media forms the largest portion of the vessel wall. Except for elastic arteries, it is composed of smooth muscle cells which are oriented circularly.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the layer indicated by the double arrow in this longitudinal section.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In this longitudinal section of a large vein (vena cava), the circular smooth muscle of the tunica media is cut in cross section. In veins, the tunica adventitia is the dominant layer of the vessel wall. In the tunica adventitia and tunica intima, the smooth muscle runs longitudinally.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The membranous septum is a component of the fibrous skeleton of the heart. It forms a portion of the interventricular septum. Below the membranous septum, the interventricular septum is composed of cardiac muscle of the myocardium.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the white blood cell in these images.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Monocyte are the largest circulating white blood cells and are characterized by a pale-staining, horseshoe-shaped nucleus and slightly basophilic cytoplasm. Monocytes leave the blood and enter the tissue, where they transform into macrophages.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Erythrocytes are, by far, the most numerous cell in blood. In normal blood they are biconcave disks and lack a nucleus.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The atrioventricular valves are composed of a central core of dense connective tissue covered on both sides by endothelium. The connective tissue core of each the valve is attached to the annulus fibrosus for that valve. The annulus fibrosus is a component of the fibrous skeleton of the heart.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cell type whose nuclei are indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In a muscular artery, as in all arteries, the tunica media forms the largest portion of the vessel wall. In a muscular artery (seen here), this tunic is composed of smooth muscle cells, which are oriented circularly around the lumen.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the double arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This image shows an electron micrograph of arteriole with 1-2 layers of smooth muscle cells. Each smooth muscle cell has an external lamina surrounding it and the plasma membrane displays many caveolae. The lumen of the arteriole is in the upper right.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The endocardium is composed of an endothelium resting on a thin connective tissue layer. This connective tissue, in turn, blends with a thicker, denser connective tissue, which composes the bulk of the endocardium. Between endocardium and myocardium is another layer, the subendocardium, composed of connective tissue containing bundle branches.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the vessel that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. In a muscular artery, the tunica media forms the largest portion of the vessel wall. It is composed of smooth muscle cells, which are oriented circularly. The presence of internal and external elastic laminae is indicative of a muscular artery. Arteries generally have thicker walls and narrower lumens compared with similarly sized veins.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the vessels indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Capillaries are lined only by an endothelium and its basal lamina. Continuous capillaries are composed of one or two endothelial cells and the surrounding basal lamina. Occluding junctions unite adjacent cells and because of their narrow lumen, these capillaries only allow erythrocytes pass through in single file. Continuous capillaries are the most prevalent type.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the vessels indicated by the rectangle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Venules have a large lumen and a thin wall. Generally, the wall consists only of the intima. Scattered smooth muscle cells are added to a tunica media as the vessel increases in size. The lumen of a venule often contains red blood cells.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the vessels shown in these images.

alternativas.feedback: Sinusoids (discontinuous capillaries) are capillaries that have wide lumens, gaps or discontinuities between adjacent endothelial cells, and a basal lamina that is interrupted or may be absent. Shown here in the liver, these modifications allow for direct access of blood plasma to the space beneath the endothelium, into which hepatocytes project microvilli.
